causal_chain: A prototype-mixture representation can preserve distinct user intents and item facets without requiring sequence data or held-out access.
An anti-collapse pairwise regularizer is needed so prototype slots do not degenerate back into a single-embedding model.
Disagreement-aware routing between user prototypes and item prototypes lets scoring emphasize the most compatible intent-facet pair instead of a global average match.

If multi-intent compression is a real bottleneck under the frozen pairwise full-sort protocol, then prototype-routed scoring should improve ranking of held-out positives, especially for users with heterogeneous histories.
Users in ML-1M often express multiple stable but partially conflicting taste facets that a single embedding compresses into one average preference direction.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that represents each user and item as adaptive mixtures over multiple latent prototypes, then scores a pair through disagreement-aware prototype routing and a residual anti-collapse pairwise objective, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 by capturing multi-intent user preference and context-free item facet diversity that single-embedding pairwise matrix-factorization-style mechanisms cannot express.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameter count or extra regularization rather than from prototype routing itself; a similarly sized static embedding model or a prototype model with uniform routing could explain the effect if routing is not the operative cause.
discriminative_predictions: A mechanism-off variant that keeps the same prototype parameters but replaces disagreement-aware routing with uniform or averaged prototype aggregation should lose a meaningful portion of any improvement.
If anti-collapse is functioning, learned prototype assignments should remain non-degenerate for a substantial fraction of users and items rather than collapsing to one dominant slot globally.

The prototype-routing model should outperform a parameter-matched single-embedding dot-product control most clearly on users with high interaction diversity, while showing smaller gains on users with narrow histories.
expected_evidence: Compared with matched control and closest parent-equivalent baselines, the full mechanism shows directional NDCG@10 improvement or at minimum a distinct subgroup pattern on heterogeneous users.
Mechanism-off ablation narrows or removes the subgroup advantage, implicating routing rather than mere capacity.
Prototype utilization statistics indicate multiple active slots across users/items, supporting the claimed representational change.
Qualification runs complete within the frozen ML-1M protocol as a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the full model fails to beat a matched single-embedding control and also fails to outperform its mechanism-off averaged-routing ablation, or if prototype usage collapses to effectively one slot for nearly all users and items, then the multi-prototype routing hypothesis is not supported in this protocol.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core representation from one latent vector per entity to adaptive mixtures over multiple learned prototypes, changes the interaction structure from single-channel dot product to routed prototype-pair scoring, and introduces an explicit anti-collapse training term. These are not profile-local operator tweaks of existing BPR-MF or LightGCN variants; they require a new executable capability in a candidate-local GeneralRecommender.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local recommender that represents each user and item as mixtures over multiple latent prototypes, scores pairs through disagreement-aware prototype routing, and trains with a pairwise anti-collapse objective will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over static single-embedding collaborative filtering because it can preserve and selectively activate multiple user intents and item facets that current profile mechanisms compress away.
implementation_requirements: Add an anti-collapse regularizer that encourages non-trivial prototype utilization and discourages all mass concentrating in one prototype slot.
Compute user-item score by combining direct residual affinity with routed prototype compatibility weighted by disagreement-aware gates derived from user/item prototype mixtures.
Implement a new RecBole GeneralRecommender with learnable user prototype logits, item prototype logits, shared prototype embeddings, and routed pairwise scoring.
Log auxiliary diagnostics such as prototype entropy and routing diversity for qualification-only interpretability.
Provide full-sort prediction over all items for evaluation without accessing held-out data during training.
Support standard pairwise BPR-style training on train-only user-positive-negative triples under the frozen protocol.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched control with similar embedding dimensional budget and pairwise training pipeline but without prototype mixtures or disagreement-aware routing, so the main difference isolated is the new representational and interaction mechanism.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace single-vector user/item representations with adaptive mixtures over multiple latent prototypes and replace simple dot-product scoring with disagreement-aware prototype routing plus residual direct affinity under pairwise ranking loss with anti-collapse regularization.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off keeps the same prototype parameterization and residual direct affinity but disables disagreement-aware routing by averaging prototype compatibilities with fixed uniform weights and removes the anti-collapse term, turning the model into a soft-capacity mixture without selective intent-facet routing.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A 4-prototype user/item mixture recommender implemented as a candidate-local GeneralRecommender, with routed prototype-pair scoring, residual direct affinity, BPR loss, and one anti-collapse regularizer, compared against a matched single-embedding control and a routing-disabled ablation on the frozen ML-1M full-sort protocol.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does a disagreement-aware multi-prototype collaborative filter recover heterogeneous user preferences better than single-embedding recommenders, yielding higher NDCG@10 through a mechanism not expressible by the current executable profile?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The model is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M is small enough for a moderate-prototype GeneralRecommender with full-sort evaluation; the main added cost is prototype routing during training/inference, which should remain tractable with a small fixed number of prototypes and standard torch vectorization.
